results.title: Authentication
excerpts:
# Authentication

How to authenticate with Pylon's API

The Pylon API uses [Bearer](rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6750#section-2.1) authentication. This means you’ll need to pass your API token in the header of your request:

```
Authorization: Bearer <token>
```

{% hint style="info" %}
Generate an API token in the [Pylon dashboard](app.usepylon.com/settings/api-tokens).
{% endhint %}

### API regions

Pylon’s API is available in two regions. Use the base URL that matches where your Pylon tenant is hosted:

* US region: <api.usepylon.com>
* EU region: <api.eu.usepylon.com>

Both regions use the same API endpoints and authentication. Configure your integration to use the region where your Pylon tenant is hosted.

You can tell a token's region from its prefix:

| Prefix          | Region |
| --------------- | ------ |
| `pylon_api_eu_` | EU     |
| `pylon_api_`    | US     |

Tokens created before prefixes were introduced have no prefix. Sending a token to the other region's API returns `401` with the `wrong_region_token` error code, and the message names the correct URL.

Once you've created a token, call the [`/me`](docs.usepylon.com/pylon-docs/developer/api/api-reference/me.md) endpoint to retrieve details about your organization and confirm your token works.

## Create an API token

Only Admins can create and manage API tokens.

1. Go to **Settings > Integrations & dev > API**. On the **Tokens** tab, click **Create API Token**.
2. Enter a **Name**.
3. Choose who the token acts as:
   * Leave **Act as user or bot (optional)** empty to give the token its own identity. Pick a **Role** to control what it can access, and optionally upload an icon.
   * Or select a teammate or bot. The token uses that user's current role and permissions.
4. Optionally, add an **IP allowlist** (see below).
5. Click **Create** and copy the token. Pylon shows it only once.

Tokens don't expire, and their access is controlled only by the role. There are no separate scopes.

### Roles

A token with its own identity uses the role you pick when you create it. You can change the role later with **Edit**. Older tokens that have no role act as Admin.

A token that acts as a user or bot has no role of its own. It always uses that user's current role, so changing the user's role changes what the token can do.

See [Roles and user management](docs.usepylon.com/pylon-docs/platform/roles-and-user-management.md) for what each role allows.

### Who actions are attributed to

* **Token with its own identity:** actions show up under the token's name and icon.
* **Token that acts as a user or bot:** actions are attributed to that user or bot.

### Bots

Bots are identities for automation, so API activity is attributed to the bot instead of to a teammate. Bots can't sign in to Pylon.

To create one, go to **Settings > Workspace > Users**, open the **Bots** tab, and click **New Bot**. Give it a name, an avatar, and a role. Then select the bot under **Act as user or bot** when you create a token.

### IP allowlist

Add IP addresses (for example `203.0.113.10`) or CIDR blocks (for example `203.0.113.0/24`) to restrict where the token can be used. You can add up to 20 entries. If the list is empty, the token works from any IP.

Pylon checks the public IP address your requests come from, so add the public egress IPs or ranges of the servers that call the API. Private addresses such as `10.0.0.0/8` or `192.168.0.0/16` never match.

A request from an address that isn't on the list returns `401` with the `invalid_api_token` error code.

excerpts:
# API

Programmatic access to read and write data in Pylon

Pylon’s API can be used to programmatically access and take action on data within Pylon.

Only Admin users can create API tokens. To learn more about Admins, see [Roles & User Management](docs.usepylon.com/pylon-docs/platform/roles-and-user-management.md).

Some common use cases for our API include:

* Fetching information about customers
* Fetching information about issues
* Creating issues programmatically

Check out our [API Reference](docs.usepylon.com/pylon-docs/developer/api/api-reference.md) for specifications on all endpoints. To call the API from TypeScript, Python, or Go, use our [SDKs](docs.usepylon.com/pylon-docs/developer/api/sdks.md), with pinned installation commands and upgrade guidance for each language.

{% hint style="info" %}
Prefer the terminal? Try our experimental [Pylon CLI](docs.usepylon.com/pylon-docs/developer/api/cli.md). It’s an early release and may change.
{% endhint %}

How do I connect to the Pylon MCP Server?

Last updated 19 days ago
The Pylon MCP server at mcp.usepylon.com provides AI tools access to your Pylon data. The endpoint uses HTTPS, so the connection is protected with TLS. It uses OAuth authentication with your Pylon account.
The application you connect to Pylon's MCP will only have access to data you would have access to in Pylon, and will read and write on behalf of you.

Common Clients

Claude Code

claude mcp add pylon --transport http mcp.usepylon.com/
Then, in Claude Code, run the /mcp command and select the pylon MCP to authenticate.
--transport http selects MCP's Streamable HTTP transport and stateless request handling; it does not mean that the connection is unencrypted or uses a plaintext HTTP URL. The Pylon endpoint remains HTTPS/TLS-protected.

Claude Desktop and Web

In "Admin Settings", add a custom connector named "Pylon" with URL mcp.usepylon.com/
Leave "OAuth Client ID" and "OAuth Client Secret" blank.
Navigate to "Settings > Connectors" and click the "Connect" button next to the Pylon MCP to authenticate.

ChatGPT

CleanShot 2026-02-19 at 20.26.36.png
In the Apps tab, search for Pylon and install our native ChatGPT app.

Cursor

Add to your Cursor MCP settings:
~/.cursor/mcp.json :
{  
  "mcpServers": {  
    ...  
    "pylon": {  
      "url": "mcp.usepylon.com/"  
    }  
    ...  
  }  
}
Navigate to "Cursor Settings > Tools & MCP" and click "Connect" next to the Pylon MCP to authenticate.

Authentication Flow

Note: The Pylon MCP server only supports OAuth authentication. API key authentication is not currently available, which may affect usage in remote environments or platforms that don't support OAuth for remote connections.
Current capabilities: The Pylon MCP server provides access to issues, accounts, and contacts, and its available tools can vary by organization and tool-specific feature flag. Registering a tool does not mean it will appear or be usable in every organization. All tool calls are also subject to the authenticated user's applicable Pylon permissions.
The MCP server does not currently support fetching notebook block content directly. To use notebook content in external tools like Claude, manually open the Account Overview notebook, copy the rendered text block output, and paste it into your conversation as context.
1. When the MCP client connects, it will open your browser
2. Log in with your Pylon account credentials
3. Authorize the MCP connection
4. The browser will redirect back and complete the OAuth flow
5. Your MCP client is now connected to Pylon!
Headless or bot-only clients: The Pylon MCP server does not currently support API keys, machine-to-machine credentials, or other non-OAuth authentication methods. If your client cannot complete the browser-based OAuth flow, it cannot connect directly to the Pylon MCP server today.
If you need token-based access for a supported integration or automation, use the Pylon REST API instead of MCP. The REST API accepts Bearer API tokens, but that authentication method does not apply to the Pylon MCP server.

description: Connect ChatGPT, Claude, and Cursor to Pylon via MCP. Work issues, accounts, contacts, and your knowledge base, scoped to each user’s permissions. title: "Pylon MCP server: connect ChatGPT, Claude, and Cursor" image: cdn.prod.website-files.com/6a2c6d7ab6674379553c0824/6ac6a7c25f73a94a812c0d67_pylon%20open%20graph%20image.png

What's New at Pylon: November
Register now
<Pylon home>

Pylon MCP server

Connect ChatGPT, Claude, and Cursor to Pylon. Work issues, accounts, contacts, and your knowledge base with the permissions you already have.
Thank you! Your submission has been received!
Oops! Something went wrong while submitting the form.

...

For ChatGPT, you can also install Pylon’s native ChatGPT app from Settings > Plugins (some older views, including very old iOS or Android apps, show Apps instead of Plugins). See how to connect Pylon to ChatGPT with MCP.
Is access scoped to each user?
Yes. Every action runs as the authenticated user. The server cannot return data that user cannot see in Pylon, or write changes that user cannot already make in the UI. Connecting needs the MCP Access permission, which the standard Member and Admin roles include.
Can engineers investigate from their editor?
Yes. Tools like Claude Code or Cursor can open a Pylon issue, pull message history, and keep working in the same flow your team already uses for debugging. Opening a pull request still depends on that coding tool’s own GitHub or codebase connection, not on a Pylon MCP "create PR" tool.
Can you turn support evidence into docs and analysis?
Yes. Feed issue context into an AI tool to draft an internal note, a product brief, or an account summary, and combine Pylon data with other sources those tools can reach (for example Notion or Linear) when those connections are configured.
How do you set up the Pylon MCP server?
Step 1
Enable MCP Access
Make sure each user or API token identity that connects has the MCP Access permission, which the standard Member and Admin roles include. Access follows the same scoping as the Pylon dashboard.
Step 2
Open the MCP Server settings in Pylon
In Pylon, go to Settings → AI Controls → MCP Server. Copy your workspace’s regional MCP URL from Installation.
Step 3
Connect your AI tool
Add the URL in your AI tool’s MCP settings, or for ChatGPT install the Pylon app from Settings > Plugins. Auth is OAuth 2.0 or an API token. Transport is Streamable HTTP (stateless).
US server: mcp.usepylon.com
EU server: mcp.eu.usepylon.com
See Pylon’s MCP docs for the full tool list.
See the MCP setup guide for client steps.
See how to connect Pylon to ChatGPT with MCP.
See how to connect Pylon to Claude with MCP.
Frequently asked questions
What is the Pylon MCP server?
MCP is an open standard that lets AI tools like ChatGPT, Claude, and Cursor connect to external products. Pylon’s MCP server exposes your Pylon workspace (issues, accounts, contacts, and more) to those tools over OAuth 2.0 or an API token, so your team can query and act on support data from the AI clients they already use.
Which AI tools can connect to Pylon via MCP?
Pylon’s MCP server works with MCP clients such as Claude Desktop, Claude Code, ChatGPT, and Cursor. For ChatGPT, the fastest path is Pylon’s native ChatGPT app; you can also add the regional MCP URL as a custom connector. Headless workers, scripts, and clients that support custom authorization headers can connect with an existing Pylon API token instead of OAuth.
What actions can an AI tool take in Pylon through MCP?
Connected AI tools can search and update issues, post internal notes, and send customer replies, which AI tools are instructed to show you for approval before sending. They can also manage accounts and contacts, draft and publish knowledge base articles, and work with macros, tags, and triggers. Tools for tasks, projects, account notes, and call recordings require Account Intelligence. Feature requests and some other tools require additional plan features. All actions stay within your Pylon permissions.
Is the Pylon MCP server secure?
Connections use OAuth 2.0 or an API token. Actions run as the signed-in user or the token’s identity, with that identity’s current role and permissions. No extra permissions are granted. The identity also needs the MCP Access permission, which the standard Member and Admin roles include.
How do I set up the Pylon MCP server?
Open Settings → AI Controls → MCP Server in Pylon, copy your regional URL (mcp.usepylon.com or mcp.eu.usepylon.com), and add it in your AI tool (or install the ChatGPT app). Sign in with OAuth, or send an existing API token in an Authorization: Bearer header if your client supports it.
Is the Pylon MCP server on every plan?
Yes. The pricing Features by tier table lists the Pylon MCP server on Professional, Advanced, and Enterprise. Some individual MCP tools still require add-ons or plan features such as Account Intelligence.

Other integrations

Pylon also connects with the other AI tools your team already uses, plus Slack, email, CRMs, and more.
 Telegram Receive and respond to customer messages from Telegram  Slack Manage B2B support directly in Slack channels alongside your team.

results.title: Pylon MCP
excerpts:
Pylon MCP

Expose Pylon data to AI tools and assistants via Model Context Protocol.

Pylon MCP Server

The Pylon MCP Server exposes Pylon data to AI tools that support the Model Context Protocol (e.g. Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor). AI tools authenticate with OAuth or an API token and can read and update issues, accounts, contacts, knowledge base articles, tasks and projects, triggers, and more within the authenticated identity's permissions.
* Server URL (US): mcp.usepylon.com
* Server URL (EU): mcp.eu.usepylon.com
* Auth: OAuth 2.0 or an API token. Actions are performed as the signed-in user or the token's identity, with that identity's current role and permissions.
* Transport: Streamable HTTP (stateless; no server-side sessions).

Setup in Pylon

Open Settings > AI Controls > MCP Server in Pylon. Copy your workspace's regional MCP URL from Installation and use it in your AI tool. For client-specific instructions, see connecting to the Pylon MCP Server.

Authentication

Both methods use the same regional MCP URL. Choose the method your client supports.

OAuth

Use OAuth with AI tools that offer an interactive connection flow. Add the regional MCP URL to your client, then sign in to Pylon when prompted. MCP requests run as the user who authorizes the connection.

API token

Use an existing API token for headless workers, scripts, or MCP clients that support custom authorization headers. You don't need a separate MCP token or an interactive sign-in.
1. Create or choose an API token.
2. Configure your client with your workspace's regional MCP URL.
3. Include this header on every MCP request:
Authorization: Bearer <API_TOKEN>
Replace <API_TOKEN> with the token value. Use mcp.usepylon.com for US workspaces and mcp.eu.usepylon.com for EU workspaces; the token must belong to the same region.
A token with its own identity uses the role assigned to that identity. A token linked to a teammate or bot uses that user's current role and permissions. The identity must have MCP Access, and each tool still requires the permissions for its operation. Any IP allowlist configured on the token also applies to MCP requests.
Some clients only support OAuth connections. Use their OAuth flow if they don't let you configure an authorization header.

What you can do with MCP today

The authenticated user or token identity needs the MCP Access permission to connect. The standard Member and Admin roles include this permission. Each tool also requires the permissions for its operation. Access follows the same scoping as the Pylon dashboard — the MCP cannot return data that the authenticated user cannot already see, or perform writes that the authenticated user cannot already write in the UI.
Some tools also require a plan feature, noted in their section. Rate limits apply per tool, elaborated below.
Use the tool names below when configuring your AI client.

...

results.title: CLI | Pylon
excerpts:
CLI

Install and use the experimental Pylon CLI
Use the Pylon CLI to access the Pylon API from your terminal or scripts.
{% hint style="info" %} The CLI is experimental. The current release is v0.1.1 and may change. The SDKs are versioned separately; upgrading an SDK does not upgrade the CLI. {% endhint %}

Install

With Homebrew on macOS or Linux:
brew install pylon-labs/tap/pylon
pylon --version
For Windows or installation without Homebrew, download an installer or binary for your platform from GitHub Releases.

Authenticate

Create a Pylon API token as described in Authentication, then run:
pylon auth login --with-token
Paste your token into the hidden prompt. The CLI saves it for future requests. On macOS, it uses Keychain when available. For automation, you can provide the token through the PYLON_TOKEN environment variable instead.
Confirm your connection:
pylon me get
Requests use the permissions associated with your API token.

results.title: How to connect Claude to Pylon with MCP | Pylon
excerpts:
Either way, Claude works on the same issues, accounts, contacts, and knowledge base you already see in Pylon, with your permissions.
This is the full setup guide. For a quick overview, see the Claude integration page and the Pylon MCP server page. Using ChatGPT instead? See How to connect Pylon to ChatGPT with MCP.

What you need before you start

* A Pylon workspace. The Pylon MCP server is listed on Professional, Advanced, and Enterprise on Pylon pricing.
* The MCP Access permission. The standard Member and Admin roles include it (roles and user management). Viewer and Integration users can't authenticate and see an "Authorization failed" error, so ask your workspace admin to change your seat type in Settings > Workspace > Users.
* Permission for each action. The MCP server can't return data you can't already see, or write anything you can't write in the Pylon UI (Pylon MCP docs).
* A Claude plan that allows connectors. Anthropic lists custom connectors on Free, Pro, Max, Ultra, Team, and Enterprise plans, and Free users are limited to one custom connector. On Team and Enterprise plans, an Owner or Primary Owner adds the connector for the organization first (Anthropic: custom connectors).

Step 1: copy your Pylon MCP URL

1. In Pylon, open Settings > AI Controls > MCP Server.
2. Copy your workspace's regional MCP URL from Installation.
The published server URLs:
* US: mcp.usepylon.com
* EU: mcp.eu.usepylon.com
Auth is OAuth 2.0 or an API token. Transport is Streamable HTTP, stateless with no server-side sessions. Actions run as the signed-in user or the token's identity, with that identity's current role and permissions (Pylon MCP docs).

Step 2, option A: add Pylon from Claude's Connectors Directory

...

1. Goes to Organization settings > Connectors.
2. Clicks Add, hovers over Custom, and selects Web.
3. Names the connector "Pylon" and enters your regional Pylon MCP URL, then clicks Continue.
4. Reviews the authentication settings Claude detected and picks how people connect under Authentication. For Pylon, use a sign-in option so each person authorizes with their own Pylon account. You don't need your own OAuth client ID or secret.
5. Clicks Add.
Then each member goes to Customize > Connectors, finds Pylon, and clicks Connect to sign in.
On an individual Pro or Max plan, go to Customize > Connectors, click + Add, then Add custom connector, and follow the same naming, URL, and authentication steps.
Once a connector is set up, you can turn it on or off for a conversation from the + button in the lower left of the chat, under Connectors.
A note on API tokens here: Claude's custom connector form can send fixed request headers, such as a bearer token. Anthropic notes that a shared credential gives everyone who uses the connector that credential's access. For people working in Claude, OAuth keeps each person acting as themselves, which is how the Claude connector signs in.

Step 2, option C: connect Claude Code

Run this in your terminal (Claude integration page, Pylon MCP docs):
claude mcp add pylon --transport http mcp.usepylon.com/
Then run /mcp inside Claude Code, select pylon, and sign in. EU workspaces use mcp.eu.usepylon.com instead. --transport http selects MCP's Streamable HTTP transport. The connection to Pylon stays HTTPS.
Headless runs and scripts.

...

FAQ

Does Pylon work with Claude over MCP?

Yes. Add Pylon in Claude from the Connectors Directory or as a custom connector, or run claude mcp add in Claude Code. Every path connects to the Pylon MCP server, and Claude acts with your normal Pylon permissions.

Where do I find my Pylon MCP URL?

Open Settings > AI Controls > MCP Server in Pylon and copy the regional URL from Installation. The published server URLs are mcp.usepylon.com for US workspaces and mcp.eu.usepylon.com for EU workspaces.

Who can connect Claude to Pylon?

Connecting needs the MCP Access permission, which the standard Member and Admin roles include. Viewer and Integration users can't authenticate. Each tool still checks the permissions for its operation, so Claude can't see or change anything you can't in Pylon.

Can I use an API token instead of OAuth?

Yes. The Pylon MCP server accepts OAuth 2.0 or an API token. The Claude connector signs in with OAuth. Claude Code and other clients that support custom authorization headers can send an existing Pylon API token as a Bearer header, as long as the token's identity has MCP Access.

Can Claude send a customer reply from Pylon?

Yes, through send_issue_reply, if your permissions allow it. A reply goes straight to the customer on the issue's channel and can't be unsent, so AI tools are instructed to show you the exact message and get your approval first.

Is the Pylon MCP server on every plan?

Yes. Pylon's pricing page lists the Pylon MCP server on Professional, Advanced, and Enterprise. Some tools also need a plan feature or add-on, such as Account Intelligence for tasks, projects, account notes, and call recordings.
See Pylon priced for your team
Seats plus agentic credits, sized to your ticket volume. No per-ticket charges.

# How do I connect to the Pylon MCP Server?

Last updated 25 days ago

The Pylon MCP server at https://mcp.usepylon.com provides AI tools access to your Pylon data. The endpoint uses HTTPS, so the connection is protected with TLS. It uses OAuth authentication with your Pylon account.

The application you connect to Pylon's MCP will only have access to data you would have access to in Pylon, and will read and write on behalf of you.

## Common Clients

### Claude Code

```
claude mcp add pylon --transport http https://mcp.usepylon.com/
```

Then, in Claude Code, run the `/mcp` command and select the `pylon` MCP to authenticate.

`--transport http` selects MCP's Streamable HTTP transport and stateless request handling; it does not mean that the connection is unencrypted or uses a plaintext HTTP URL. The Pylon endpoint remains HTTPS/TLS-protected.

### Claude Desktop and Web

In "Admin Settings", add a custom connector named "Pylon" with URL `https://mcp.usepylon.com/`

Leave "OAuth Client ID" and "OAuth Client Secret" blank.

Navigate to "Settings > Connectors" and click the "Connect" button next to the Pylon MCP to authenticate.

### ChatGPT

In the Apps tab, search for Pylon and install our native ChatGPT app.

### Cursor

Add to your Cursor MCP settings:

`~/.cursor/mcp.json` :

```
{
  "mcpServers": {
    ...
    "pylon": {
      "url": "https://mcp.usepylon.com/"
    }
    ...
  }
}
```

Navigate to "Cursor Settings > Tools & MCP" and click "Connect" next to the Pylon MCP to authenticate.

## Authentication Flow

**Note:** The Pylon MCP server only supports OAuth authentication. API key authentication is not currently available, which may affect usage in remote environments or platforms that don't support OAuth for remote connections.

**Current capabilities:** The Pylon MCP server provides access to issues, accounts, and contacts, as well as knowledge base articles and collections, macros, tags, and triggers. Tools for tasks, projects, and account notes require Account Intelligence. Available tools can also vary by organization and tool-specific feature flag. Registering a tool does not mean it will appear or be usable in every organization. All tool calls are also subject to the authenticated user's applicable Pylon permissions.

The MCP server does not currently support fetching notebook block content directly. To use notebook content in external tools like Claude, manually open the Account Overview notebook, copy the rendered text block output, and paste it into your conversation as context.

1. When the MCP client connects, it will open your browser

2. Log in with your Pylon account credentials

3. Authorize the MCP connection

4. The browser will redirect back and complete the OAuth flow

5. Your MCP client is now connected to Pylon!

**Headless or bot-only clients:** The Pylon MCP server does not currently support API keys, machine-to-machine credentials, or other non-OAuth authentication methods. If your client cannot complete the browser-based OAuth flow, it cannot connect directly to the Pylon MCP server today.

If you need token-based access for a supported integration or automation, use the Pylon REST API instead of MCP. The REST API accepts Bearer API tokens, but that authentication method does not apply to the Pylon MCP server.

## Session Expiry and Reconnecting

OAuth sessions expire periodically. The exact duration varies by MCP client - some sessions last a few hours, others can last several days.

When your session expires, you may see authentication errors or your MCP tools may stop returning results. To reconnect, simply re-authenticate through the same flow you used during initial setup:

* **Claude Code:** Run `/mcp` and re-authenticate the Pylon connection
* **Claude Desktop/Web:** Go to **Settings > Connectors** and click "Connect" next to Pylon
* **Cursor:** Go to **Cursor Settings > Tools & MCP** and click "Connect" next to Pylon

## Pylon MCP Server

The Pylon MCP Server exposes Pylon data to AI tools that support the Model Context Protocol (e.g. Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor). AI tools authenticate with OAuth or an API token and can read and update issues, accounts, contacts, knowledge base articles, tasks and projects, triggers, and more within the authenticated identity's permissions.

* **Server URL (US):** `https://mcp.usepylon.com`
* **Server URL (EU):** `https://mcp.eu.usepylon.com`
* **Auth:** OAuth 2.0 or an API token. Actions are performed as the signed-in user or the token's identity, with that identity's current role and permissions.
* **Transport:** Streamable HTTP (stateless; no server-side sessions).

### Setup in Pylon

Open **Settings > AI Controls > MCP Server** in Pylon. Copy your workspace's regional MCP URL from **Installation** and use it in your AI tool. For client-specific instructions, see connecting to the Pylon MCP Server.

### Authentication

Both methods use the same regional MCP URL. Choose the method your client supports.

#### OAuth

Use OAuth with AI tools that offer an interactive connection flow. Add the regional MCP URL to your client, then sign in to Pylon when prompted. MCP requests run as the user who authorizes the connection.

#### API token

Use an existing API token for headless workers, scripts, or MCP clients that support custom authorization headers. You don't need a separate MCP token or an interactive sign-in.

1. Create or choose an API token.
2. Configure your client with your workspace's regional MCP URL.
3. Include this header on every MCP request:

Replace `<API_TOKEN>` with the token value. Use `https://mcp.usepylon.com` for US workspaces and `https://mcp.eu.usepylon.com` for EU workspaces; the token must belong to the same region.

A token with its own identity uses the role assigned to that identity. A token linked to a teammate or bot uses that user's current role and permissions. The identity must have **MCP Access**, and each tool still requires the permissions for its operation. Any IP allowlist configured on the token also applies to MCP requests.

Some clients only support OAuth connections. Use their OAuth flow if they don't let you configure an authorization header.

### What you can do with MCP today

The authenticated user or token identity needs the **MCP Access** permission to connect. The standard Member and Admin roles include this permission. Each tool also requires the permissions for its operation. Access follows the same scoping as the Pylon dashboard — the MCP cannot return data that the authenticated user cannot already see, or perform writes that the authenticated user cannot already write in the UI.

# How to connect Claude to Pylon with MCP

Connect Claude and Claude Code to Pylon over MCP: setup steps, OAuth or API token auth, permissions, what Claude can do, and safe first workflows.

Pylon Team

·

5 min read

You can connect Claude to Pylon in a few minutes through the Pylon MCP server. In Claude, add Pylon from the Connectors Directory and sign in with your Pylon account. In Claude Code, it's one command. Either way, Claude works on the same issues, accounts, contacts, and knowledge base you already see in Pylon, with your permissions.

This is the full setup guide. For a quick overview, see the Claude integration page and the Pylon MCP server page. Using ChatGPT instead? See How to connect Pylon to ChatGPT with MCP.

## What you need before you start

* **A Pylon workspace.** The Pylon MCP server is listed on Professional, Advanced, and Enterprise on Pylon pricing.
* **The MCP Access permission.** The standard Member and Admin roles include it (roles and user management). Viewer and Integration users can't authenticate and see an "Authorization failed" error, so ask your workspace admin to change your seat type in Settings > Workspace > Users.
* **Permission for each action.** The MCP server can't return data you can't already see, or write anything you can't write in the Pylon UI (Pylon MCP docs).
* **A Claude plan that allows connectors.** Anthropic lists custom connectors on Free, Pro, Max, Ultra, Team, and Enterprise plans, and Free users are limited to one custom connector. On Team and Enterprise plans, an Owner or Primary Owner adds the connector for the organization first (Anthropic: custom connectors).

## Step 1: copy your Pylon MCP URL

1. In Pylon, open **Settings > AI Controls > MCP Server**.
2. Copy your workspace's regional MCP URL from **Installation**.

The published server URLs:

* US: `https://mcp.usepylon.com`
* EU: `https://mcp.eu.usepylon.com`

Auth is OAuth 2.0 or an API token. Transport is Streamable HTTP, stateless with no server-side sessions. Actions run as the signed-in user or the token's identity, with that identity's current role and permissions (Pylon MCP docs).

## Step 2, option A: add Pylon from Claude's Connectors Directory

This is the fastest path in Claude on the web and desktop (Claude integration page):

1. **Open the Connectors Directory.** Click the + button in the lower left of your chat, or type /, then hover over Connectors and select Manage connectors. Click + next to Connectors to open the directory. You can also get there from Customize > Connectors.
2. **Find Pylon.** Browse by category or scroll the list, select Pylon, and click Connect or Install. On Claude Team and Enterprise plans, an Owner or Primary Owner adds the connector for your organization first.
3. **Authorize.** A sign-in window opens. Sign in with your Pylon account and approve access.

## Step 2, option B: add Pylon as a custom connector

Use this if your organization prefers to manage the connector itself, or you need the EU URL. Steps follow Anthropic's current guide (custom connectors).

On Team and Enterprise plans, an Owner or Primary Owner (on Enterprise, also anyone with a custom role that includes Manage access to Libraries):

1. Goes to **Organization settings > Connectors**.
2. Clicks **Add**, hovers over **Custom**, and selects **Web**.
3. Names the connector "Pylon" and enters your regional Pylon MCP URL, then clicks **Continue**.
4. Reviews the authentication settings Claude detected and picks how people connect under **Authentication**. For Pylon, use a sign-in option so each person authorizes with their own Pylon account. You don't need your own OAuth client ID or secret.
5. Clicks **Add**.

Then each member goes to **Customize > Connectors**, finds Pylon, and clicks **Connect** to sign in.

# Authentication

How to authenticate with Pylon's API

The Pylon API uses [Bearer](rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6750#section-2.1) authentication. This means you’ll need to pass your API token in the header of your request:

```
Authorization: Bearer <token>
```

{% hint style="info" %}
Generate an API token in the [Pylon dashboard](app.usepylon.com/settings/api-tokens).
{% endhint %}
